inputs.original_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to renegotiate the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, warning of an indefinite nationwide strike if talks fail. It is telling that workers have to threaten disruption before their long-standing demands are treated as urgent: institutions depend on their labor, yet too often leave them without a fair hearing. The government should negotiate in good faith and reach a just agreement, rather than casting workers’ defense of their rights as the problem.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to renegotiate the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, warning of an indefinite nationwide strike if talks fail. That workers must threaten disruption to get a long-standing agreement taken seriously says a lot about whose labor institutions value—and whose grievances they can afford to ignore. University staff deserve a fair hearing and a just agreement; the government should negotiate in good faith instead of treating workers’ collective action as the problem.
